The gyil is a West African xylophone, a tuned idiophone, H-S classification 11/12 gong, bell, xylophone and lithophone system. It is built with seventeen keys mounted over gourds, struck by the player with wooden mallets with rubber heads. It belongs to the music of the Dagara and Birifor peoples of northern Ghana and southern Burkina Faso, and is usually played by two people in pairs with a kuor gourd drum; one person can also accompany with drum and mallet at once. Players are mostly men, but there is no restriction of sex.

It is usually played by two people in pairs with a kuor gourd drum, and one player may also play it, accompanying with the drum and part of the mallet. For a beginner the first job is the basic order: hold the mallets, strike the keys, and fit what you play to the drum.
